what: LM-MULTI (2026-10-19): the 1,000-step language-model run at four threads with BF16-ATTN and with a hundred steps a run call (FACTS-RUN, MULTI-STEP) -- LM-PAIRED's five seeds (20261011, 1001, 2002, 3003, 4004), four arms a seed in one session, their order rotated seed by seed: BCIR under bf16+exp+reduce+attnbf16 a hundred steps a run call (bcir-attnbf16-k100), under bf16+exp+reduce+attn a hundred steps a call (bcir-attn-k100) and one step a call (bcir-attn-k1, LM-PANELS's bcir-panels arm), and torch.compile with fused AdamW under torch.autocast(cpu, bfloat16) (torch-compiled-bf16). The analysis was fixed before the runs (paired_multi.py's docstring): per pair of arms the ratio of the median warm steps per seed, their geometric mean and a 95% Student-t interval on the log ratios, and a +-0.01-nat margin on the test cross-entropy difference for every pair but bcir-attn-k100 / bcir-attn-k1, which is one state and held to equality instead; whether those two end in one state seed for seed, and whether bcir-attn-k1 ends in LM-PANELS's bcir-panels states.
host: 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz container (family 6 model 207: AMX-BF16 and AVX512-BF16; the instance of ../ and ../../../2026-10-18/panels/lm/), GCC 13.3 (the trainer builds), PyTorch 2.13.0 at four intra-op threads, Python 3.11.15 (the declared floor); every record names commit 418c5c2, the tree's runtime/c identical to it (library da56782ef09f, one build for both BCIR contracts); indicative wall times, no PMU
reading: Median warm step, BCIR with the bf16 attention a hundred steps a call / PyTorch bf16 / BCIR's binary32 attention a hundred steps a call / the same one step a call: seed 1001 68.9 / 154.1 / 69.4 / 67.4 ms; seed 2002 66.4 / 146.1 / 65.8 / 67.0 ms; seed 3003 63.9 / 150.9 / 65.0 / 66.1 ms; seed 4004 64.1 / 157.3 / 67.9 / 68.9 ms; seed 20261011 65.8 / 153.6 / 68.5 / 65.4 ms (14,870-16,029 tokens a second with the bf16 attention, 6,508-7,011 for PyTorch). Quality, the claim the run exists for: the bf16 attention's test cross-entropy is 0.00006 nats above compiled PyTorch bf16's on average (95% interval -0.00157 to +0.00169), validation -0.00071 (-0.00354 to +0.00211), inside the +-0.01 margin, and 0.00117 below the binary32 attention's (-0.00298 to +0.00064; validation +0.00108, +0.00002 to +0.00214), inside it too. Speed: BCIR with the bf16 attention trains at 2.315 times PyTorch bf16's tokens a second (95% interval 2.194-2.444, faster on 5 of 5); the binary32 attention one step a call, LM-PANELS's pair again in this session, 2.276 (2.201-2.353, 5 of 5; 2.282 there). The two gains measured inside one process are not resolved across processes: the bf16 attention over the binary32 one reads 1.023 (0.991-1.056, faster on 4 of 5), where the step pairs read 1.029 (1.018-1.042); a hundred steps a call over one 0.995 (0.958-1.032, 3 of 5), where FACTS-RUN's rotated arms read 1.048 for ten-step calls. Each arm here is its own process, and the A/A controls of ../ show a process's placement moving a library's time by up to about 3%, so five seeds cannot resolve a gain of about 3%: the intervals are that wide. States: the hundred-steps-a-call arm ends in the one-step arm's state on 5 of 5 seeds (a call of a hundred steps is a hundred calls of one) and the one-step arm in LM-PANELS's bcir-panels states on 5 of 5 (FACTS-RUN, ATTN-SOFT and BF16-ATTN's binary32 path keep every bit over 1,000 steps). Peak RSS 496-534 MB on every BCIR arm, the arena (362,944,768 bytes) and workspace (11,534,592: at this shape the GEMM groups' packs exceed the bf16 attention's regions) the same with and without the bit, against 1,128-1,151 MB for PyTorch; the persistent state 157,390,848 bytes on every arm. PyTorch's compile and first steps took 10.2-11.8 s, 44.4 s on the session's first seed (a cold inductor cache), outside the warm median.

files.run.sh: the rounds as run (bash run.sh OUT TORCH_PYTHON DATA_SRC from the repository root, DATA_SRC LM-PANELS's prepared seeds: preparation is deterministic for a seed); a BCIR arm's record is removed before its run and a run that leaves none stops the rounds
files.paired_multi.py, summary.json: the analysis fixed before the runs, and its output over runs/ (--previous LM-PANELS's summary.json, ../../../2026-10-18/panels/lm/summary.json)
files.runs/{bcir-attnbf16-k100,bcir-attn-k100,: the twenty train records (train_comparison.py's train stage): losses, gradient norms, every step's seconds, the evaluations, the final validation and test metrics, the state digest, peak RSS and the memory split
